findings: Stable recommended prebuilt customizable native sheet for most apps across iOS, Android and React Native SDKs, using automatic, vertical or horizontal layout and an Appearance API controlling fonts, colors, borders and shadows without implying arbitrary layout redesign. The UI renders/localizes detail collection, can show Apple Pay and Link express wallet buttons, and supports dynamic display/order and A/B testing, 100+ catalog access, Dashboard and Custom Payment Methods. Old raw lines 4-12, 17-27 and 34-62; new raw lines 5-19, 30-40 and 47-75. Concept lines 12-24 distinguish its packaged confirmation from Flow Controller’s merchant-controlled confirmation and Payment Element’s embedded presentation.

Both captures document saving, displaying and managing cards, US bank accounts and SEPA debit, automatic consent collection, configuration of CustomerSessions API controls (save-consent box, list visibility, removal and last-method protection), billing identity/contact collection, CVC recollection and card-brand filtering (old raw lines 64-92; new raw lines 77-109). Access to a saved method is distinct from paying now or future successful charge. New raw lines 38-40 and the separate mobile overview lines 86-127 distinguish PaymentIntent payment, SetupIntent without initial payment, and PaymentIntent with setup_future_usage for paying and saving. The main Payment Sheet capture specifies no API/SDK minimum, endpoint sample, secret, webhook sequence or terminal lifecycle.

The historical April iOS Embedded Payment Element save guide lines 109-132 and 621-632 distinguishes server resource creation and scoped CustomerSession access/client secrets from payment-result events including processing, succeeded and failed. These sibling implementation details illustrate the state boundary and stay attached to that route. A UI demo, method display, setup, consent, or a pending state establishes neither completed payment nor fulfillment eligibility.

Mapped source lines 13-56 contain the durable April behavior with abbreviated CustomerSessions controls and saved-card CVC wording. Its 50+ appearance count has independent older and November mobile overview support, although neither matched Payment Sheet capture gives that count. No need to fabricate an April Accounts v2 or address-autocomplete claim from silence.

The dedicated contemporaneous guide says Android only on compatible NFC-equipped Android devices, request-access private preview (companion lines 9-35). Treat the unanchored all-platform line as ambiguous, not evidence of expansion. The prior and newer US Android native purchase note and iOS app-to-web Checkout pointer match in substance.

This is the sheet’s full billing-address collection, distinct from partial collection and the separate mobile Address Element integration.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/payment-sheet, both the April 22 capture (old raw lines 4-39 and 41-92) and the November 7 capture (new raw lines 5-52 and 54-109) describe Stripe’s recommended prebuilt, customizable Payment Sheet for most iOS, Android and React Native apps. The in-app UI provides automatic, vertical or horizontal layout, Appearance API styling, localized forms, dynamic method display/order and A/B testing, Dashboard or Custom Payment Methods, and possible Apple Pay and Link express buttons. Access to over 100 methods is catalog access. Both document saving cards, US bank and SEPA debit, automatic UI consent collection, optional CVC recollection on a saved payment method and card-brand filtering. CustomerSessions API controls the save checkbox, saved-list visibility and method removal, including protecting the last method. November explicitly requires Customer objects for this native sheet and excludes customer-configured Accounts. Customer identity and CustomerSession access are distinct from PaymentIntent payment or SetupIntent without an initial charge. The US Android digital-goods note allows in-app Payment Sheet and points iOS to app-to-web Checkout. Tap to Add is a separate access-request private preview, explicitly Android-only with compatible NFC hardware in its dedicated November guide. Both captures allow configurable billing name, email, phone and address; November adds supported-country full-address autocomplete with no additional setup and Google Maps policy conditions. source-stripe-inapp-payment-sheet.md captures most of April’s stable behavior and uses a separately supported appearance count. It omits November’s identity, preview and autocomplete boundaries and compresses saved-method controls and CVC scope.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/payment-sheet, compare old raw lines 8-39 and 64-92 with new raw lines 9-52 and 77-109 when updating source-stripe-inapp-payment-sheet.md. Substantive November clarifications are native Payment Sheet Customer-only identity, disclosure of the access-request Tap to Add private preview, and Stripe autocomplete for full billing addresses in supported countries with no extra setup. Google Maps Platform Acceptable Use Policy applies, with possible disablement or other action. Carry reciprocal route warnings for the ambiguous “This feature is available across all supported platforms” and the contemporaneous dedicated guide’s explicit Android-only compatible-NFC-device private preview, and for Customer-only native Payment Sheet versus the dated Embedded Payment Element Account-or-Customer server route and general Accounts v2 or hosted Checkout guidance. Keep the separately scoped 100+ Payment Sheet catalog and 40+ mobile dynamic display counts and the automatic consent UI alongside merchant compliance obligations. Date April’s US Android/iOS app-to-web note, demo and legacy links, and preserve its raw provenance. App Clip versus download QR is demo navigation, the address link changes from an iOS payment-element route to payment-sheet, the saved-method link drops the iOS qualifier and setup moves to accept-payment type=setup. CDN assets, wording and generic layout labels establish neither an SDK version change nor deprecated integrations. Keep Customer, CustomerSession, PaymentIntent and SetupIntent separate, and scope integration version/secret/event details to linked implementation authority. Method visibility, customer consent, setup and a UI result cannot establish completed payment or settlement.
